agent_notes: The superscription is verse 1 in the Hebrew (KJV 56:0). 'Jonath-elem-rechokim' is rendered as a tune title ('The Dove of Silence among Strangers' in the dramatic layer) following the traditional reading 'dove of silence of the distant ones'; the vocalization אֵלֶם 'silence' versus אֵלִים 'gods/mighty ones' (an old emendation) is uncertain, so the literal layer keeps the transliteration plus a bracketed gloss. Miktam is left untranslated; 'inscription/engraving' (from כתם 'gold') is a guess, not a settled meaning.

agent_notes: The refrain ends with אָדָם 'man/anyone' where verse 5 has בָשָׂר 'flesh' (so Radak: 'adam and basar are one'). The KJV renders both with different verbs of anxiety; I keep the contrast flesh/man visible.

Revised after review: 'and wine' is dropped. BDB/HALOT citations are replaced by Radak (zivchei toda) and the Targum (qurbanei todan). Malbim's reading is given as the alternative to 'vows owed to you': that God made the vows to David through the prophets. The five English versions split between 'praises' (KJV, Webster), 'thank-offerings' (YLT, ASV) and BBE's paraphrase; I follow YLT/ASV because Radak and the Targum both read sacrifice.

agent_notes: הֲלֹא is read as an emphatic rhetorical question ('Have you not…?') with the verb of the first clause carried over (ellipsis), as Radak takes it ('הלא לשון חוזק'). KJV's 'wilt not thou deliver' turns it into a future petition, which the Hebrew perfect הִצַּלְתָּ in the first clause makes less natural. The Qere/Ketiv is not at issue. 'Light of the living' (so KJV, YLT, ASV) kept over BBE 'light of life'; the plural חַיִּים is retained.

Malbim's identification of the two vows with the Samuel and Gad promises, and Rashi's 'return to the Land of Israel', are Davidic-biographical readings from the superscription tradition; I cite them but do not build the translation on them.

I use 'gasp after/pant for' in the literal layer to keep the sense of hungry snapping, and say so in the commentary; the sense is disputed between 'snap at', 'swallow' and 'trample'.

agent_notes: The Hebrew string for this verse ends with a stray word אֵין (token 9, marked X), which belongs to no sense in this verse (it is a Masoretic/Sefaria artefact, likely a verse-end marker or a misplaced word from the following text). I glossed it '[stray: not]' and left it out of both translations. The verse is also hard: the first clause 'because of wickedness, deliverance for them' is usually taken as a question ('Shall they escape because of their wickedness?', KJV, ASV, Radak) but could be a statement (YLT) or emended. I follow the question reading in the dramatic layer and keep the elliptical Hebrew in the literal layer.
